cards.text: Jesus just healed a man's withered hand on the Sabbath, and the scribes and Pharisees are filled with rage. They're talking with one another about what they might do to Him. Then, in those days, Jesus goes out to the mountain.

cards.question: Jesus heads out to the mountain. What does He go there to do?
Up on the mountain, Jesus prays for a little while and heads back down before dark.

cards.text: When daylight comes, Jesus calls His disciples to Him and starts picking some of them out. He prayed ALL NIGHT before this, friend. I can't even stay awake through one batch in the oven.

cards.question: Out of all His disciples, Jesus chose ___ of them.
Jesus gives the twelve He chose a title too. What does He designate them?

cards.text: Then come the names: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew, James and John, Matthew, Thomas and more. Count 'em up and you get two Simons, two Jameses and two Judases. Name tag day must have been WILD. And the last name lands heavy: Judas Iscariot, "who became a traitor."

Then Jesus comes down with them to a level place, where a large crowd of His disciples and a great number of people from all over Judea and Jerusalem are waiting. Friend, my whole planet is one bakery big, so this crowd would be standing on my ROOF.

cards.question: Some of the people in the crowd at the level place came from as far as the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.
Why did this great crowd come to Jesus?

answers.text: To hear Him and be healed

cards.question: People troubled by unclean spirits were in that crowd too. They had to leave without being healed.

cards.text: Now the whole crowd is pressing in close around Jesus. Only crush I've ever seen like that is a room full of bakers the second I pull a fresh tray out of the oven.

cards.question: The entire crowd at the level place was trying to ___ Jesus.
Why is the whole crowd trying to touch Jesus?

answers.text: Power from Him was healing every one of them
They hoped He would pick them as apostles too
They believed it would keep away future sickness

findings.problem: The setup line says the crowd is 'pressing in close around Jesus' right before card 13 asks what the crowd was trying to do to Him. Pressing in close points almost straight to 'touch' and rules out 'see' and 'follow', so the setup gives the answer away. 'Pressing in close' is also not in the text. Luke 6:19 says only that the crowd 'was trying to touch Him.' The card should set up the moment without describing the physical push toward Him.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 7 is the summary card for the name list (Luke 6:14-16) and runs 4 sentences: the names, the count of repeated names, a joke, and Judas Iscariot. The bite-sized rule says every story card after the opening card is 1 to 2 sentences, and it treats a summary card as one beat. But the doc's own good summary example (Genesis 5) is also 4 sentences.
findings.question: Does the 1 to 2 sentence limit apply to summary story cards for long stretches, or can a summary card run longer, like the Genesis 5 example in prep-walkthrough.md? If it can run longer, is there a sentence limit?
